parts.text: Child mental health issues have been rising in the UK over the last decade. This was exacerbated by the COVID

and continues to be a concern, particularly around issues such as sedentary lifestyles and excessive screen time.

In a new study, colleagues and I have found that visiting a local park

had a measurable impact on child mental health.

Throughout childhood and through adolescence, children are developing their social and emotional skills. This social-emotional development provides the

for good mental health. Failing to reach typical milestones such as developing social skills and friendships provides an indication of a child’s current mental health, as well as their mental health in later life.

This means that finding ways to

and encourage healthy social-emotional development is a way to improve child mental health and give them the foundation for good mental health throughout their lives.

Having green and natural spaces close to people’s homes is one factor which
studies have shown is linked with improved child mental health. These spaces are thought to improve child mental health by encouraging healthy
. For example, they encourage physical activity, socialising and imaginative and adventurous play. Research suggests that being in natural spaces can have

and stress-reducing effects for both children and adults.

Much of the research related to green spaces and child mental health has been cross-sectional study designs. This means that the study

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Regular park visits are associated with measurable differences in children's mental health.
Schools can reduce some learning gaps while advantages linked to family wealth persist.
Adults' responses to risk and mess can limit the benefits children gain from outdoor play.
Science curricula often overlook women whose work helped shape scientific knowledge.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: In a new study, colleagues and I have found that visiting a local park regularly had a measurable impact on child mental health.

questions.prompt: What did the park study examine?
options: Only the number of cars sold in a city
The effects of deep-space travel on adults
The relationship between regular local park visits and child mental health
Whether parks can replace every school subject
questions.explanation: 第 2 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: In a new study, colleagues and I have found that visiting a local park regularly had a measurable impact on child mental health.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is explicitly made in paragraph 6?
options: In a new study, colleagues and I have found that visiting a local park regularly had a measurable impact on child mental health.
Much of the research related to green spaces and child mental health has been cross-sectional study designs.
Child mental health issues have been rising in the UK over the last decade.
We found children tended to display better mental health during periods when they went to parks more often compared to when they went less.
questions.explanation: 定位第 6 段，比较四个选项的具体信息。其余选项来自本文其他段落，并非本段明确陈述的内容。
questions.evidence: Much of the research related to green spaces and child mental health has been cross-sectional study designs.

questions.prompt:

“We found that children who were taken to the park at least once a week from six months to 11 years old scored, on average, 16.5% better on their mental health assessments compared to those who were taken less than once a week over the same period.”
options: Paragraph 10
Paragraph 5
Paragraph 3
Paragraph 11
